themes.consensus_view: Most banks still expect AI spending to drive growth and earnings into 2027, but after the steep sell-off in chip and AI stocks the question has moved from how much companies spend to who actually earns a return, with hyperscalers and AI users favored over hardware suppliers and with debt-funded AI spending drawing more doubt.

facts_agreed.claim: Banks now judge AI by which companies earn a return on it rather than which spend the most, and favor the large cloud providers and companies using AI to lift revenue or margins.
evidence_quotes: the narrative is shifting from who can invest the most to who can capture the highest returns
we recommend investors own the hyperscalers.
a growing share of the opportunity may belong to the adopters
AI adoption remains a high conviction theme from us into 2027

facts_agreed.claim: AI and data center investment is expected to remain a main source of economic growth.
evidence_quotes: We expect AI investment to remain a source of growth.
AI investment will likely remain the main driver of global trade in 2027-28
we expect the data center buildout to continue
the relatively concentrated nature of growth does create some vulnerability

facts_agreed.claim: The borrowing that funds AI spending is growing and investors are charging more for it.
evidence_quotes: investors are increasingly penalizing AI’s financing intensity
2027 will be the year when chip financing dominates
any move to a more conservative approach will have tightening implications

facts_agreed.claim: Several assumptions behind this year's AI trade are being tested at once, which keeps AI stocks volatile.
evidence_quotes: several assumptions underpinning this year’s AI trade are being tested simultaneously
monetisation doubts risk keeping AI hyperscalers volatile
AI-capex risks, high market concentration, relative valuation premiums and elevated volatility

facts_contested.claim: Whether AI capital spending keeps growing or is peaking
facts_contested.for_evidence: we expect the data center buildout to continue
facts_contested.against_evidence: capex growth is halving, data centers face a political veto

facts_contested.claim: Whether the large cloud providers are a good place to hold AI exposure while payback is unproven
facts_contested.for_evidence: hyperscalers are the "vol adjusted" best place for your investing dollar
facts_contested.against_evidence: monetisation doubts risk keeping AI hyperscalers volatile

themes.consensus_view: Most banks expect the Fed to raise rates by a quarter point in December and again around March 2027, lifting the top of its policy rate to about 4.5%, while Allianz warns that markets have historically priced in fewer hikes than the Fed went on to deliver.

facts_agreed.claim: Several banks expect the Fed to raise rates at its December meeting, with hot October inflation keeping the hike on track.
evidence_quotes: We continue to expect a 25-bp hike in December
the path is clear for the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) to raise rates in December
further action to raise the target range for the Federal funds rate
confirms our view that the Fed will raise rates in the near term

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs expects another hike in March after December, its third of the cycle.
evidence_quotes: we continue to expect a third hike in March

themes.consensus_view: Data centers are the one part of US construction still growing fast and are holding up the whole building cycle, but state and local political pushback after the midterms, plus power and permit limits, is the open risk to how far the buildout can go.

facts_agreed.claim: Data center building is the main support of the US construction cycle and also a concentration risk because so much of the growth depends on it.
evidence_quotes: The segment is both the main support of the cycle and a concentration risk.

facts_agreed.claim: Several desks flag state and local political pushback, including new governors in Texas, Ohio and Georgia and moratorium fights after the midterms, as slowing data center approvals and expansion.
evidence_quotes: State and local governments slowing data center expansion
Newly elected governors restricting data center approvals in Texas, Ohio, Georgia
Data center moratorium fights
Post-midterm policy headwinds for data centers
Data centre power and permit supply constraints

themes.consensus_view: Banks across nine desks treat the Iran and Middle East conflict as an oil price shock that is feeding inflation and central bank policy, while some see the shock already fading on peace hopes; nobody has staked a primary directional view.

facts_agreed.claim: Several banks flag the Iran and Middle East conflict as an energy price shock that passes through into inflation and pushes the Fed and ECB toward tightening.
evidence_quotes: Fed and ECB new tightening cycle driven by Middle East energy prices
Iran war energy cost pass-through to inflation
Energy shock and inflation peak in Q1 2027
Middle East conflict energy price shock

facts_agreed.claim: Some banks note the energy shock easing as peace talks and Middle East optimism pull prices lower, even with tanker attacks near Hormuz.
evidence_quotes: Iran war energy shock fading
Declining energy prices on Middle East optimism
Iran conflict peace talks and oil price uncertainty
Hormuz tanker attacks yet crude falls

themes.consensus_view: Most banks expect the Fed to raise rates again because inflation is staying high, with Morgan Stanley and Crédit Agricole calling quarter-point hikes in December and March, while Raymond James thinks markets are pricing more hikes than the Fed will deliver.

facts_agreed.claim: Sticky inflation means the Fed is likely to raise rates again in the coming meetings.
evidence_quotes: we see risks as tilted to the upside
we expect two additional rate hikes from the Fed with 25bp increases in December and March
All of this suggests that the Fed may need to raise rates again

facts_agreed.claim: A hawkish Fed is pressing on while growth signals weaken, pushing short-term yields up relative to long-term ones.
evidence_quotes: first, a flatter curve, as hot inflation and a hawkish Fed
the November/December 2018 parallels feel increasingly close

facts_contested.claim: How much more tightening the Fed will deliver
facts_contested.for_evidence: we expect two additional rate hikes from the Fed with 25bp increases in December and March
facts_contested.against_evidence: Markets may be overestimating how much additional tightening the Fed will need to deliver

themes.consensus_view: Banks across five desks track record bond borrowing by the big cloud companies to pay for AI data centers, and Goldman and ZeroHedge note that the bonds tied to this build-out are trading worse than the wider corporate bond market, but nobody has staked a directional view yet.

facts_agreed.claim: Allianz, HSBC Asset Management and Morgan Stanley flag record investment-grade bond issuance by the large cloud companies to fund AI spending.
evidence_quotes: Hyperscaler AI capex bond issuance versus sovereign supply
Record US investment-grade issuance from big tech
Hyperscaler unsecured issuance and IG supply record

facts_agreed.claim: Goldman Sachs and ZeroHedge flag that debt tied to hyperscalers and data centers is moving more than the broader corporate bond market, with data-center spreads (the extra yield over Treasuries) widening and funds underweight data-center junk bonds.
evidence_quotes: Hyperscaler credit basket at 2x beta vs IG100
HY datacenter bond underweights among funds
Data-center credit spreads widening

themes.consensus_view: Six desks reference Anthropic's record IPO and the selling in tech stocks that followed it as a live market event, but none has staked a directional view on the stock or its effect on the market.

facts_agreed.claim: Several desks flag the Anthropic IPO, from its opening trade to its effect on demand for AI stocks, as a market event this week.
evidence_quotes: Anthropic IPO with CA-CIB as joint bookrunner
Anthropic IPO as sign of AI equity appetite
Anthropic IPO opening print and market reaction
Anthropic IPO greenshoe exercised in full
Nasdaq 100 inclusion of Anthropic Dec 21

facts_agreed.claim: Two desks link the record-size IPO to the decline that followed in the stock and in tech shares more broadly.
evidence_quotes: Anthropic record IPO and subsequent slide
Anthropic IPO hangover driving global tech liquidation
